label: pre-converge 2026-08-24, before the observable night (expectations judged)

sec-transport-mariadb-clients.why: goes DONE (encrypted). Mechanism VERIFIED in the running image 2026-08-24, and it is not the one ce457cb2 named: the env-watcher starts after 30-laravel init and inotifywaits from that point, so it can never see the init-time write. The carrier is the init sequence itself — /container/init/init.d/40-freescout:41-44 runs laravel_env_passthrough (ENV_ prefix confirmed default, SETUP_TYPE defaults AUTO) then freescout:clear-cache (re-caches, ClearCache.php:53) + config:clear — and config/database.php:56 consults env('DB_MYSQL_ATTR_SSL_CA'). Current .env has 0 occurrences of the key, so the whole delta is the recreate. If this stays not-encrypted:freescout, check FIRST that compose actually recreated the container.

notify-supersede.why: stays restated:39 — corrected from 'change to ~36', which was wrong twice over, both measured: (1) all 4 unread drift rows carry supersede_key NULL and Bone retires only WHERE supersede_key = ? (wing.py:544; the 01:02 backup's own precedent — keyed emit, zero unkeyed retired), and (2) drift-watch will not emit tonight at all — it alerts only on pending_critical>0 or a stale scan, and the queue holds 0 pending CRITICAL with the scan 17h old against a 336h threshold. The backlog (31 os-resume, 5 backup-verify, 3 drift) retires only by another reconcile-inbox pass once each emitter has a keyed successor — tomorrow's deliberate act, not tonight's mechanism. A DROP means someone ran the reconciler; a rise to 40 means the queue gained a CRITICAL overnight and drift-watch fired. Side-prediction not gradeable here: tonight's 01:02 backup should produce the FIRST emit-time retirement ever — the keyed 2026-08-24 01:02:56 row gets superseded_at; check it with a SELECT in the morning.

sec-transport-pg.why: stays DONE, saying `encrypted`. It is the control: nothing in this converge touches PostgreSQL clients, so a change here is a sampling artefact or a regression, and either is worth more than the green.

sec-transport-hedgedoc.why: stays DONE. Its answer comes from HedgeDoc's own kernel, not a sample, so unlike sec-transport-pg it should not be able to flap at all. If it does, the self-test is not as deterministic as claimed.

sec-transport-mysqld-exporter.why: stays `plain`. Nothing was written for it. A change would mean somebody edited the exporter outside the repo — which is how two services went down on 2026-08-23.

sec-transport-mariadb.why: stays 1 (require_secure_transport OFF). The repo now DECLARES it off (roles/pazny.mariadb compose command, --require-secure-transport=0), so the converge re-asserts the declared value; rung 4 waits for freescout (tonight) and the exporter (not yet written). A flip to 0 here means the requirement went ON outside the repository — the exact 2026-08-23 out-of-band SET GLOBAL shape that took FreeScout down behind a healthy healthcheck.

sec-backrest-auth.why: stays 1 (auth disabled). The live config.json is seed-once (force:false) — the converge cannot reconcile it, and the fix is a deliberate act (live reconcile + bcrypt mint) that has not been built. This hold is the OPEN-item control: if it flips to 0 overnight, something mutated live daemon config unattended, which is worse news than the red it would clear.

reader:red.why: head falls 2 red -> 1 red when the loop's nightly pass lands REM-214/REM-217 in the tree. An UNMET here means a THIRD consecutive [re-judge] — at that point the finding is about the loop driver, not the rows: read tools/loop-status.py before anything else. (The earlier claim that the inbox line falls by ~3 as drift retires its own is withdrawn — see notify-supersede: no drift emission tonight, and a keyed emit cannot retire unkeyed rows.) A NEW red is still the night's most valuable output.

reader:containers.why: stays `0 not-clean`. 61 containers, all running and healthy at record time; the converge recreates several around 22:00 and every one must be back and HOLDING healthy by morning. This line exists because on 2026-08-22 Nextcloud and FreeScout were both down and no reader said so — container health was nobody's declared source. Total-count changes do not move this head by design; only a container that is not running-clean does.
